eventName: The Shop That Would Not Sleep
provenance: New fan-written event dialogue, informed by existing character dialogue. Not recovered original-game text.

recommendedNPC.name: Tirami
recommendedNPC.role: Brings a caravan order that exceeds her stall's overnight capacity; contributes expert brewing and packing work, keeps the commercial records, and delivers the finished shipment.
recommendedNPC.basis: Tirami is an accomplished brewer and proud commercial rival. The event puts her competence and accountability into tension with the need to collaborate, without portraying her as incapable.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: If I wash one more bottle, I'm naming it and sending it home.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: That makes five children you've sent away tonight.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Then I hope there's room for a sixth.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Tirami? We're closing.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: The caravan leaves at dawn. Their quartermaster added an amendment to my order.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: How large an amendment?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: This page. And this little page folded inside it.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You can brew the potions. You just can't fit that many batches through one cauldron.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Exactly. I've brought the ingredients and my brewing schedule. I need your spare cauldron.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: And the contract?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: My seal. If a bottle fails, the caravan comes to me.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Then every batch needs its maker in the ledger. We should be able to trace a fault.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I wasn't planning to lose track.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Neither was I.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You can argue while we carry the crates. The room won't grow larger on its own.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: This is bench-sharing. Not a rescue.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Good. Then take the heavy end.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Keep the sealed supplies by the conveyor until the cauldron's clear. We need the scales.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Where do I put the ledger?

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Not on my blanket. I brought that for inventory night, not as a packing cloth.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Tea after the first batch. We're going to need it.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I can make my own tea.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You can. But mine's already hot.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Fine. Just leave 'sleepover' off the invoice.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Hold the label still. The ink hasn't dried.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: That's my merchant's seal you're about to smudge.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: It's covering the batch initials.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: My name goes on the front. I answer for the order.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Then let the maker's name sit somewhere a clerk can actually find it.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: You think I don't understand how to trace a bad batch?

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: I think this bottle has been between you for a minute and is still unlabeled.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: The outer tag can take my seal. Put your initials inside the packing ledger.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Fine. I'll rewrite the column headings.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: And, Tia? Your last tray passed my seal check. Every bottle.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: I expected it to. ...Thank you for checking.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Lovely. Now may I have my bottle back?

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Wait. My count is six short.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Check the rack beside the window.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: That's supposed to hold bottles awaiting their seals.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: It does. Six of them. I moved the rack so the corks could finish setting.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: You could have told me.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: You asked me not to interrupt your count.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: I could hear that count from the storeroom. Shall I bring the rack over?

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: No. Leave it until the seals are ready. The six are accounted for.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Then both of you, sit for five minutes. The cauldron won't run away.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: I can sit and supervise.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I'll watch the rack. You can close your eyes until the next batch.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Wake me before the ledger needs signing.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I wouldn't dare forge handwriting that difficult.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: I'll bring the biscuits. There were some left when we started.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: The caravan's gone. I stood at the gate with an empty crate.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Did the quartermaster ask for an explanation?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: He didn't need to. I'll send one anyway. I accepted an amendment I couldn't fulfill.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Come in before you freeze. The kettle's still warm.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Tea won't put bottles on that cart.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: No. But you can write to them with warm hands.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Make the letter precise. What was ordered, what we finished, and what couldn't be shipped.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Zero is a remarkably easy quantity to record.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: The quantity, yes. The wording may take longer.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: ...Will you read it before I send it?

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: We'll set another cup out. Write first; breakfast can wait a few minutes.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: There's room on the cart for everything I couldn't finish. Too much room.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: And the receipt states exactly what we delivered. No guessing later.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I tied a ribbon around the smallest shipment of my career.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You tied it carefully.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I was trying to make it look less lonely.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: It secures the label. Its feelings are irrelevant.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: The label is staying put, at least.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I'll tell the caravan master what we couldn't finish. He may be less polite than this crate.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Take the ledger copy. It will save you arguing over the count.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Thank you. Don't clear my cup yet.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: I wasn't going to.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: A respectable shipment. Not the full order, but the numbers agree.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: The quartermaster signed for it without complaining. He did ask who brewed which batches.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: And did you tell him?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I gave him the ledger. It's what a ledger is for.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: You rewrote the heading.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: The old one was too small. Three names hardly fit.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You managed to make yours fit before.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Pio, please. I've been awake all night.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: You also corrected the batch numbers beside my initials. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: They deserved to be correct. Now, is there anything left of the tea?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: The caravan asked where to send its next large order.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Please tell me you didn't promise them tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I told them to ask both shops for a quotation. A quotation, Pio. Not a promise.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: You actually wrote 'both shops'?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Twice. The quartermaster was half asleep, and I wanted him to remember.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You didn't have to do that.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I wasn't going to volunteer your labor a second time. You can decide what it's worth.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Good. And this time we'll calculate the hours before accepting.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I had hoped you would forget that part.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: Sit down. We can argue about rates after breakfast.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I wasn't arguing. I was negotiating.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Every crate boarded. The quartermaster checked the amended order twice.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: And the count?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Exact. He asked how we managed it before dawn.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You had your schedule ready to show him, I suppose.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I did. He asked whose changes were written in the margins.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I told him to ask you. He wrote your name down, along with Pio's.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: You gave him all three names?

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: He was going to order again. I thought he'd better know who could actually do the work.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: You mean who could stay awake long enough.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: If I let go of this packing list, I may fall over.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: You're already sitting. You've been holding it upside down.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: Then I'm making sure nobody alters the figures.

lines.speaker: Pio
lines.text: There's a clean blanket on the chair. The figures can sleep alone.

lines.speaker: Tirami
lines.text: I should really get back to my stall.

lines.speaker: Tia
lines.text: After breakfast. We saved you a cup, and I'm not entering a missing teacup in that ledger.
